name: France
terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
keyfacts: Vin de France replaced Vin de Table and allows the grape variety and vintage to be shown on the label.
IGP basically replaced Vin de Pays, and former VDQS wines had to qualify as AOP or be downgraded to IGP.
If a single varietal name is used on a French label, the wine must be made from a minimum of 85% of that variety.

blurb.text: France is one of the world's largest wine producers, with several hundred appellations that set grapes and winemaking by place. It gave the world grapes such as Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah. Merlot, Ugni Blanc and Grenache are its most planted.
